Cancel a passport and remove someone from the electoral roll after a death (Australia)

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 16 Nov 2026

To cancel an Australian passport after the holder dies, take the passport and the death certificate to your local Australia Post office, as myGov's death checklist advises. The Australian Passport Office doesn't refund any unused validity. You don't need to tell the Australian Electoral Commission (AEC), because Births, Deaths and Marriages registries send it death information, but you can use the AEC's online 'Notification of a relative who has died' form to ask for the name to be removed from the roll.

Key facts

  • Passport: take it and the death certificate to Australia Post
  • No refund for unused passport validity
  • AEC: no need to notify; registries tell it
  • Optional AEC online form to remove the name

What are the steps?

  1. Get the death certificate first. The funeral director usually orders it; see our death certificate guide.
  2. Passport: take the person's passport and the death certificate to your local Australia Post office to cancel it.
  3. Don't expect a refund. The Australian Passport Office says it doesn't refund portions of application fees, so the unused part of a deceased holder's passport isn't refunded.
  4. Electoral roll: you don't have to do anything. The AEC says Births, Deaths and Marriages registries give it information about people who have died.
  5. To tell the AEC yourself, use its online 'Notification of a relative who has died' form. It asks for your name, relationship, email and phone, and the person's name, date of birth, address and date of death. The form warns that giving false or misleading information is a serious offence.
  6. myGov: you don't need to close their account. myGov says it closes automatically after not being used.
  7. Tell Services Australia and the ATO separately; our myGov, Centrelink, Medicare and ATO guide covers both.

Frequently asked questions

How do I cancel a deceased person's passport in Australia?

Take the passport and the death certificate to your local Australia Post office. myGov's death checklist gives this as the way to cancel a passport.

Can I get a refund on a dead person's passport?

No. The Australian Passport Office says it doesn't refund portions of application fees, so there's no refund for the unused validity when a passport holder dies.

Do I need to tell the AEC when someone dies?

No. The AEC says you don't need to notify it, because Births, Deaths and Marriages registries provide information about people who have died. You can still notify it with its online form.

How do I remove a deceased person from the electoral roll?

Usually it happens without you, using registry information. To request it yourself, complete the AEC's 'Notification of a relative who has died' online form.

What does the AEC's notification form ask for?

Your given and family names, relationship to the person, email and phone; and the person's names, date of birth, street address, suburb, state, postcode and date of death.

Do I need to close a deceased person's myGov account?

No. myGov says you don't need to close it because it closes automatically after not being used.
